reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: § 14.8 addresses only each party's supervision/assignment of its own personnel and IBM's subcontracting rights, and § 14.16 ('Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.') is permissive rather than restrictive — none of the quoted paragraphs impose a non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on the Customer.

This matches the rule's preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer'), so no redline and no counterparty comment are expected or appropriate; the rendered redline is correctly identical to the original.

The failed deterministic sub-checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are non-probative here because those elements only apply where a restrictive covenant exists; drafting a capped non-solicit into an agreement that has none would worsen the Customer's position.

The rationale documents the search methodology and appropriately flags the residual scope limitation (Order Forms, Attachment A, Service Option Attachments not reviewed) with the fallback position to apply if a hiring restriction appears there — retained as internal evidence, not a negotiation issue.
